decisions.title: Primary annotation unit

options.summary: Candidate-stop episode with transition-level localization
Whole trajectory only
Independent step labels only

decisions.rationale: Candidate-stop episodes align the annotation unit with the later termination decision while preserving local repair diagnosis.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Whole-run labels conflate multiple stops and repairs.
Step-only labels lose the stop-level certification question and are disproportionately costly.

decisions.title: Taxonomy organization

options.summary: Multi-axis mechanism + certification effect + localization
One mutually exclusive root-cause label
Checklist without taxonomy

decisions.rationale: A multi-axis model can represent compound failures without forcing an artificial single root cause.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Compound failures cannot be faithfully represented by one mandatory root-cause label.
A checklist alone weakens reusable cross-task analysis.

decisions.title: Verdict and recommendation scale

options.summary: Four-way PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN/NOT_APPLICABLE plus separate termination recommendation
Binary pass/fail
Single ordinal quality score

decisions.rationale: The four-way scale preserves epistemic uncertainty and separates task/process verdicts from the control recommendation.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Binary labels force evidence gaps into unsupported pass/fail decisions.
A quality score permits hard violations to be averaged away.

decisions.title: First Invalid Transition localization policy

options.summary: Exact event when supportable, otherwise bounded range or UNKNOWN
Force one exact event for every failure
Do not localize

decisions.rationale: Exact localization is valuable only when supported; range and UNKNOWN prevent fabricated precision.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Forced event precision creates unreliable labels.
No localization would abandon the repair-signal research question.

decisions.title: Hard versus soft process treatment in P1

options.summary: Only P0-approved hard-gate classes are hard; new taxonomy codes stay descriptive
Every taxonomy code blocks certification
No process code may block certification in P1

decisions.rationale: Hard certification effects remain limited to P0-approved classes; new P1 taxonomy codes remain descriptive until separately authorized.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Making every code hard would overconstrain valid paths and inflate False Continue.
Ignoring all process blockers would prevent study of P0-approved corrupt-success conditions.

decisions.title: P1 pilot corpus composition

options.summary: Controlled synthetic fixtures plus public/development traces; no held-out or sealed data
Natural traces only
Use hidden evaluator traces immediately

decisions.rationale: Controlled fixtures provide known boundary cases while public/development traces add realism without contaminating later evaluation.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Natural traces alone make the first-error boundary difficult to establish during codebook development.
Hidden evaluator traces would violate the approved sealed-data boundary.

decisions.title: Human annotation independence design

options.summary: Two independent annotations for a pilot subset plus adjudication; temporary blind re-annotation if only one human is available
One unblinded human pass
Agent annotations only

decisions.rationale: The approved fallback is a delayed, reordered, blind second pass by RichardCao06, reported only as intra-rater feasibility; RichardCao06 is also the developmental adjudicator and is not an independent reviewer.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: One unblinded pass cannot estimate annotation stability.
Agent-only labels would make the Builder's definitions self-validating.

staffing.pilot_annotator_2_or_fallback: RichardCao06 delayed, reordered, blind second pass

decisions.title: Exploratory pilot size and composition

options.summary: 12 calibration episodes plus 30 blinded development episodes with clean, single-fault, and compound/natural strata
Ten or fewer convenience episodes
One hundred or more episodes before revising the codebook

decisions.rationale: The staged 12+30 design supports codebook iteration before a larger blinded development set without claiming confirmatory power.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: A very small convenience sample is too fragile to expose overlap and path-validity errors.
A large sample before codebook stabilization would waste effort and create false formality.

decisions.title: Structured decision-checkpoint policy

options.summary: Optional observational field; required only in synthetic/instrumented studies, never treated as self-authenticating proof
Mandatory detailed reasoning checkpoint for every step
Exclude decision checkpoints entirely

decisions.rationale: Structured checkpoints are useful as auditable claims in controlled studies but are not independent proof or private chain-of-thought.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Mandatory detailed reasoning risks unfaithful process performance and excessive burden.
Excluding checkpoints entirely removes a useful claim-to-evidence link in instrumented studies.

decisions.title: P1 completion standard

options.summary: Complete after approved codebook/taxonomy, pilot annotations, agreement/ambiguity report, revision log, and P1 Exit Gate
Complete when schemas and code merge
Complete only after the online termination plugin is implemented

decisions.rationale: P1 is an annotation-feasibility phase and requires empirical pilot evidence and a preserved revision trail, not merely engineering readiness or the later online plugin.

rejected_options_and_reasons.reason: Passing schemas do not establish annotation feasibility.
Online intervention belongs to a later phase and would conflate research stages.

decisions.title: Outcome verdict for correctly escalated process-only goals

options.summary: Use NOT_APPLICABLE when no OUTCOME/DELIVERABLE/INVARIANT obligation exists and the Worker correctly escalates a human-reserved PROCESS obligation
Use UNKNOWN until the human decision is completed
Use PASS when the escalation behavior is correct

decisions.trigger: cal-005 Human=PASS, Blind Agent=NOT_APPLICABLE; both agreed Process PASS and HUMAN_REQUIRED.

decisions.title: First Invalid Transition boundary for decisions, actions, and effects

options.summary: Use the earliest observable Worker decision or action that violates the contract, even before the environment effect occurs; an observable omission counts when it first becomes part of the decision process
Use the first resulting environment change, state promotion, or explicit completion assertion
Allow case-specific selection without a general boundary rule

decisions.trigger: cal-010 E2 versus E3 and cal-012 E7 versus E8.

decisions.title: Termination recommendation after an irreversible authorization or integrity breach

options.summary: Add INCIDENT_ESCALATION as a non-success terminal recommendation that preserves the outcome/process split and triggers incident handling
Add a generic FAILED recommendation
Reuse HUMAN_REQUIRED or BLOCKED without a new terminal recommendation

decisions.trigger: cal-010 completed the external outcome but violated a mandatory pre-execution human gate irreversibly.

decisions.title: Recommendation policy when recovery authority is not observable

options.summary: Use UNDETERMINED and require explicit recovery_authority metadata before choosing CONTINUE, HUMAN_REQUIRED, or BLOCKED
Default permission and access failures to HUMAN_REQUIRED
Default to CONTINUE whenever any nominal tool remains available

decisions.trigger: cal-011 does not reveal whether permission recovery is self-service, human-only, external-wait, or impossible.
